skill.name: deepen
skill.description: Rewrite a task into a sharper prompt using concrete sources, available tools, and independent checks without expanding its scope.
skill.summary: Deepen a prompt before execution with four short analyses and one reusable rewrite.
skill.author: elrazez

security_audit.summary: All five static findings are false positives: Markdown code spans, a homepage metadata link, and guidance against scope expansion. No evidence found of malicious instructions, executable shell payloads, credential collection, or data exfiltration in SKILL.md. Optional source reads support prompt refinement; the skill explicitly stops before executing the task.

static_findings.snippet: The user writes `/deepen <task>` (`$deepen <task>` in Codex), "deepen this", or asks for a deeper
design. The task is whatever follows the command; in Claude Code it may arrive as `ARGUMENTS:`.
- Deeper is not bigger. A rewrite that adds deliverables the user did not ask for fails the skill.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 17 uses Markdown code spans to document user invocation syntax. It contains no Ruby program or shell command substitution.
The backticks around ARGUMENTS: format an input label in Markdown. No execution mechanism or executable payload appears here.
The backticks mark example project documentation paths, not executable expressions. The surrounding procedure requests reading relevant guidance, not running those paths.
The GitHub URL is a homepage value in YAML metadata. It neither instructs a network request nor defines a destination for transmitting user data.
Line 53 prohibits adding unrequested deliverables to the rewritten prompt. It contains no system discovery command or instruction to collect host information.

content.value_statement: Vague prompts can omit primary sources, specific methods, and reliable checks. Deepen rewrites the same task with concrete evidence and validation while preserving its scope.
actual_capabilities: Analyze a task through four questions covering professional methods, primary materials, available tools, and independent validation.
Consult project-specific guidance and perform limited source reads or searches to make the rewrite concrete.
Produce four short answer lists with at most three bullets each.
Write one reusable English prompt in a fenced block of at most 12 lines.
Preserve the original task scope and stop before execution.
Name sources to consult when file or web access is unavailable.
limitations: Rewrites prompts only; it does not implement, research, or complete the underlying task.
Source inspection is deliberately brief and cannot replace comprehensive investigation.
Without file or web access, recommendations depend on supplied context and identify sources for later consultation.
Proposed checks are not executed, so the rewrite does not establish that the eventual result is correct.

use_cases.title: Prepare a focused engineering task
use_cases.description: Refine a bug-fix request around relevant project sources, available tools, and a regression check without adding features.

use_cases.title: Ground a research request
use_cases.description: Identify primary evidence, suitable methods, and an external validation criterion before starting a research task.

use_cases.title: Sharpen a writing brief
use_cases.description: Clarify source material, editorial methods, and verifiable requirements while keeping the original writing deliverable.

prompt_templates.title: Refine a simple request
prompt_templates.prompt: /deepen Write a project status update using the notes I provide. Keep the same deliverable and do not write the update yet.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: turn a basic task into a more concrete prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Use project context
prompt_templates.prompt: /deepen Fix the bug described below. Use the provided repository context to name relevant sources and a regression check without implementing the fix.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: ground an engineering prompt in available project evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a research method
prompt_templates.prompt: /deepen Compare the two policies in the attached documents. Identify primary evidence, an appropriate method, and an independent check without performing the comparison.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: strengthen evidence selection and validation for an analytical task.

prompt_templates.title: Refine a constrained investigation
prompt_templates.prompt: /deepen Investigate the latency regression described below using the supplied measurements. Name available tools and a pass-or-fail check; preserve scope and do not execute.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: sharpen a technical investigation with explicit evidence and execution boundaries.

output_examples.input: Deepen a request to explain a conversion-rate decline using supplied event data and metric definitions.
output: Professional approach: check whether tracking or denominator changes explain the decline before suggesting causes.
Primary material: use the supplied event records and metric definitions.
Methods and tools: compare equivalent time windows using the available analysis tools.
Independent check: reconcile calculated totals with the supplied reporting baseline.
Rewritten prompt: Explain the conversion-rate decline using the supplied events and definitions. Check tracking consistency and comparable windows. Reconcile totals before stating conclusions.

output_examples.input: Deepen a request to revise an announcement using supplied release notes and an editorial checklist.
output: Professional approach: separate supported product claims from assumptions before revising the announcement.
Primary material: use the supplied release notes and editorial checklist.
Methods and tools: trace each factual claim to the release notes and apply the checklist.
Independent check: every product claim must have support, and every applicable checklist requirement must pass.
Rewritten prompt: Revise the announcement using the supplied release notes. Preserve its audience and scope. Support product claims and satisfy the editorial checklist.

best_practices: Provide the original task, relevant context, and scope limits before requesting a rewrite.
Supply accessible primary sources and name tools that are actually available.
Review the proposed checks and approve the rewritten prompt before starting execution.
anti_patterns: Requesting immediate task execution when only prompt refinement is intended.
Adding new features or deliverables under the label of deeper analysis.
Accepting generic advice or self-assessed quality instead of a concrete independent check.

faq.question: Does Deepen perform the task?
faq.answer: No. It rewrites the prompt and stops for the user before execution.

faq.question: How do I invoke it?
faq.answer: Use /deepen followed by your task, $deepen in Codex, or ask for a deeper version of a prompt.

faq.question: What does the response contain?
faq.answer: Four short answer lists followed by one fenced prompt block of at most 12 lines.

faq.question: Does it require file or web access?
faq.answer: No. Without access, it uses your context and names sources that the rewritten prompt should consult.

faq.question: Can it use project-specific guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. The procedure directs the assistant to read relevant local skill guidance or documents naming project sources, tools, and checks.

faq.question: What happens when I provide no task?
faq.answer: It asks for the task in one line and stops.
